title: Count Prefix and Suffix Pairs II
summary: Given a 0-indexed array of string words, count the number of index pairs (i, j) where i < j and word at index i is both a prefix and a suffix of the word at index j.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array of string words, count the number of index pairs (i, j) where i < j and word at index i is both a prefix and a suffix of the word at index j.
constraints: Count ordered index pairs i<j where words[i] is both a prefix and a suffix of words[j].
Repeated words at different indices count as distinct pairs.
hints: Pairing the next front and back characters lets one trie path represent being a prefix and suffix simultaneously.
Insert earlier words into a trie keyed by (front character, back character), adding terminal counts while scanning each new word.
For each word, walk zipped forward/reversed characters; add terminal count at every depth; mark the final node terminal.
At depth d the path matches exactly the first and last d characters, so every terminal encountered is precisely one earlier border word.
editorial: At depth d the path matches exactly the first and last d characters, so every terminal encountered is precisely one earlier border word.

tests.explanation: The word a borders each of the three later words, and aba borders ababa, giving four pairs.
Pa borders papa and ma borders mama; neither short word borders the other family.
